The descriptor family's fsyncs are the port's unconditional-fsync divergence from TS's writeFileAtomicSync (fsync opt-in, never requested at these call sites), and TS has no boot-registration write at all. Cutting the spawn record's pre-rename fsync (the TS persistWorker call shape) and the boot-registration write entirely (in-memory only) removes 2 of the 5 fsyncs and 1 of the 3 descriptor writes per fresh create while keeping the create-completion fsync as the metadata-survival barrier.

parity_notes:
TS anchors: daemon-supervisor.ts persistWorker (writeFileAtomicSync with { mode: 0o600 } only - the fsync is opt-in and never requested at the descriptor call sites) and the absence of any worker_register command (TS has no boot-registration write at all). Frozen surfaces untouched by construction: no session-JSONL rows, no RLM API/wire/tool schemas, no prompts, no TUI output bytes - the daemon's descriptor write policy is not observable on any client surface. The create-completion persist (launch_worker's post-create write) KEEPS the durable write_file_atomic as the metadata-survival barrier (Ready + rootSessionId + sessionFile + createCommand.sessionPath durable before the create response reaches the client - the barrier the create's own sessionFile check and the RLM spawn admission rely on). The supervisor-config and update_prepare sites keep the durable write (the rejected daemon-boot cut is not resurrected; update_prepare out of scope). Tests: write_file_atomic_unsynced_replaces_an_existing_destination + persist_worker_unsynced_stamps_and_round_trips (the TS shape: atomic rename + the fresh updated_at stamp + temp cleanup) + a_known_resident_registration_writes_nothing_to_disk (the registration refreshes the resident in memory - lifecycle Ready, live socket, instance id - while the on-disk spawn record stays BYTE-identical; the create-completion persist owns the next durable state).

CRASH-WINDOW AMENDMENT (the review wave's request + R4's standing analysis, 2026-10-01 ~22:30Z): the spawn-record row of the crash-window matrix under-reported the torn-file cost. THE HONSENT SENTENCE: a torn/empty descriptor after a power crash loses the descriptor's WHOLE payload — the recoveryJournalPath AND the durable create_command — so the boot scan's parse skips it inert (no journal-based revival, no create replay; the session reopens through the client create). The pre-change port's synced persist_worker did not have this window (the overwrite was durable: old-or-new, both parseable); TS's own unsynced persistWriter (daemon-supervisor.ts:1748-1752, writeFileAtomicSync with no fsync option at any descriptor site) carries the IDENTICAL window on every descriptor write — the finding is the convergence itself, not a divergence. The parity verdict is unaffected (TS-identical by construction); the open question is the product-durability policy (retain the spawn-site fsync as a deliberate strengthening vs accept the TS posture) — the review wave's disposition presents both options to the operator. No verdict changes; this amendment names the payload-loss honestly.
